Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: photorealistic interior design mockup, one full-frame portrait photograph, no collage.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the actual existing entrance hall. Preserve its camera position, framing, perspective, and narrow spatial proportions. Make a convincing photographic edit of THIS room, not a newly invented similar hall.
Design: a restrained warm Arts and Crafts entrance for a Victorian Bedford Park house, using decor only.
LOCKED EXISTING FEATURES: keep the exact front door shape and white paint, its tulip stained glass with curved green lower bands, the clear rectangular fanlight and visible exterior lantern, narrow tulip stained-glass sidelight to the RIGHT, brass letterbox and latch, all existing pale grey wall and white panelling colours, ornate cornice, existing three ribbed clear glass pendants, black steel glazed lounge door on left, actual intricate grey/black/ivory geometric star mosaic floor tiles with original scale and pattern, dark wood demi-lune console with turned legs and drawer at right and its hammered dark rectangular mirror. Preserve the cropped stair newel at the right foreground. Do not change any architectural openings or dimensions, do not widen hall, do not redesign console or enlarge mirror. Keep glass reflections plausible.
Make ONLY these decor changes:
1. Remove the existing white coat pole, pink towel, small clutter/clock/boxes from console, and coat on foreground newel.
2. Put a slender freestanding dark walnut timber coat tree in the existing narrow nook in front of the right sidelight, with a restrained simple vertical stem, 3 short rounded wooden arms with aged brass tips, compact stable roughly 32-35 cm wide weighted base, about 170 cm tall. It is an understated slim timber design, NOT a sprawling Thonet/bentwood stand or wall hooks. Show just ONE lightweight muted olive everyday jacket and one neat dark dog lead; leave most stained glass visible. Keep base entirely in nook, not the doorway.
3. Retain existing wicker rectangular lidded Fortnum and Mason hamper at actual size, relocate it neatly underneath the console between its legs if physically plausible; do not shrink basket or enlarge table to force it. Leave feet and walk route clear.
4. Console top holds exactly three things: at the end nearest front door a SMALL warm aged-brass table lamp with an oatmeal linen tapered shade, approximately 35 cm total high and 19 cm shade diameter, no tall oversized lamp; at far end a modest compact aspidistra with arching broad dark green leaves in an earthy terracotta pot around 16-18 cm diameter, plant kept around 40 cm overall high rather than towering over mirror; between them a small shallow patinated brass key dish. Respect the narrow tabletop, do not place objects in midair, and let mirror remain usable.
5. Replace entrance doormat with a simple natural coir rectangle with narrow dark brown border, approximately door width, same general location as current mat. Keep most star-pattern tiles exposed; no floor runner in entrance square.
Lighting: realistic soft daylight through existing glass with a small warm lamp glow, modestly lift exposure to see objects while retaining original paint colours. Real timber grain, woven shade, coir fibres, wicker and exact tile detail. Editorial interior photograph, realistic lived-in home, no drawing, no CGI polish.
No added benches, joinery, sconces, new ceiling fixtures, flowers, people, writing, labels, arrows, watermarks, borders or dimension callouts. Deliver a single clean portrait photo.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: photorealistic interior design mockup, one full-frame portrait photograph, no collage.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the actual existing narrow hallway from front door looking past stair to kitchen and garden. Retain EXACT camera framing, perspective, apparent stair pitch and narrow walk route. Produce a photographic decor edit of this photo, not a generic period hallway.
LOCKED EXISTING FEATURES: existing oak treads and risers and their dimensions, white turned newel and balusters, dark brown handrail, pale grey walls and white picture-frame stair mouldings, tall flush cupboards opposite stair with the SAME door seams, cornice and ceiling shapes, downlights and detector, black steel glazed lounge door at right, door and transom into rear kitchen, kitchen and garden view beyond. Preserve EXACT intricate grey/black/ivory geometric star mosaic tile floor in every uncovered area, at the original pattern scale; do NOT swap to diamond tiles or wood. No painting, no new architecture, no changed doors, no extra stair widths.
Make ONLY these decor changes:
1. Remove jacket from newel, cap on stair and any temporary foreground bag/clutter. Existing stair and architectural shapes remain untouched.
2. Fit a wool stair runner in a softly muted clay/rust terracotta with tiny tone-on-tone herringbone texture and narrow dark tobacco-brown binding, approximately 62-65 cm wide on roughly 89 cm stair treads. Centre on actual stair. It covers the tread and riser centres, follows every existing step tightly with credible professional fitting and realistic weave. Show oak bands roughly 12 cm wide on each side. NO brass stair rods in this quieter version; no stair reshaping or added treads.
3. Place a separate understated hall flatweave runner down the narrow tiled route between stair and cupboards. Warm flax/oatmeal field, fine woven texture, a slim subdued rust woven border, no bold medallions or busy motifs, no tassels. About 60 cm wide and 240-270 cm long conceptually, scaled to the actual photo, with visible continuous tile strips both sides. It begins alongside/just beyond stair foot, leaving the entrance foreground tiled, and stops BEFORE rear doorway leaving a tiled landing. Lies flat, not up the stairs or under cupboard door leaves. It complements rather than exactly matches the rust stair runner.
4. Add three modest coordinated framed botanical studies on warm ivory paper within the EXISTING upper stair wall moulding panels at left, rising with stairs. Fine botanical illustrations of stylised foliage in olive, muted russet and charcoal, subtle Arts and Crafts influence, restrained and realistic. Slim dark walnut frames, cream mounts, about 25x35 cm to 30x40 cm each, proportioned to actual available panels; keep every original moulding intact and no frames straddling mouldings. A coherent group rather than three unrelated statement artworks. At most three frames, those beyond crop can be partly cropped naturally.
Lighting: natural existing daylight from kitchen/garden, with exposure gently balanced so original unchanged wall paint reads accurately. Photorealistic interior photograph, textured wool, visible oak grain and exact original star tiles. Understated warmth with a clear unobstructed sightline to garden.
No people, text, captions, labels, arrows, watermarks, borders, floating objects, wall sconces, new furniture or changed rooms. Single clean portrait photograph.
